name: Threaded evidence wall
purpose: Connect seemingly separate evidence through a moving camera
looks_like: Dark grey felt wall with tilted white-bordered photos pinned in; a red string runs between pins and the camera drifts across the wall.
use_when: 'Six separate pieces of evidence, a receipt, a burner phone, a security tape, a letter, a ledger and a key, all pointed at one man.' -> photos:6
'Individually, the leaks looked harmless. Put together, they described a cover-up.' -> photos:6
'Every contract, email and bank transfer led back to the same shell company.' -> photos:6
avoid_when: A sentence about one person or one photo; beats under 5 s (the camera needs time to move).
With a central person and photos around them use case-board; this one has no centre, only a connected wall.

name: Borders in focus
purpose: Explain neighboring territories with progressive boundary emphasis
looks_like: Dark map of Europe with Poland, Belarus and Ukraine outlined in red and each tagged with a small black name label.
use_when: 'Poland, Belarus and Ukraine all share a border, and all three felt the shockwave.' -> country (2-4 countries named) + data
'Germany sits between France, Poland and Austria, and it has fought all three.' -> country list + data
'The new tariffs hit Canada and Mexico first, the two countries that touch the American border.' -> country list + data
avoid_when: Only one country (use country-trace); no countries named.
Needs map data (data); a plan without --allow-data skips it. Use country-outlines when the countries are not neighbours.

name: Person and place
purpose: Associate a person with a highlighted region
looks_like: Dark map (Arabian peninsula) with one country filled red and a portrait on the left of it.
use_when: 'Sultan Qaboos ruled Oman for fifty years.' -> one_name + country + photo:1
'Born in Brazil, Pele became the face of the sport.' -> one_name + country + photo:1
'The founder, Elon Musk, grew up in South Africa.' -> one_name + country + photo:1
avoid_when: A sentence with no country; a group of people; a country without a person. For rulers specifically use sovereign-profile.
Use this when the person is tied to a place (born there, from there, ran it); not for a general bio.

name: A place in time
purpose: Link a territory, location pin and historical date
looks_like: Dark map with the USA filled red, a big white condensed date '12 June 1900' at the top and a small black pin label with the same date on the map, 'Where it happened' at the bottom.
use_when: 'On 12 June 1900, in the United States, the first of the raids began.' -> country + date + data (pin)
'In 1066, England was invaded.' -> country + date
'On the fourth of July, 1776, America declared independence.' -> country + date
avoid_when: A sentence with a date and no country, or a country and no date (use date-center or country-trace); several dates.
Needs data (pin location); skipped without --allow-data.

name: Distribution dots
purpose: Show many locations inside a region
looks_like: Dark world map zoomed on North America with the USA filled blue and about 25 red dots scattered over it.
use_when: 'The chain now has 1,400 stores spread across all fifty states.' -> country + number
'The gang had cells in more than twenty American cities.' -> country + number
'Fans watch the team in 38 countries.' -> country + number
avoid_when: No country, or a number that is money or a percent; one single location (use city-marker).
The dots are generic and carry no labels: do not use when the sentence names specific cities (use route-line or map-callout).

name: Regional share
purpose: Place an animated percentage in geographic context
looks_like: Dark Europe map with a black circle and a red ring about 37% full showing '37%' sitting over Germany.
use_when: 'Germany alone accounts for thirty-seven percent of the continent's exports.' -> percent + place + data
'Forty percent of the world's cocoa comes from Ivory Coast.' -> percent + place + data
'California makes up 12 percent of all US sales.' -> percent + place + data
avoid_when: A percent with no place; money or counts; several places.
Needs map bounds data; skipped without --allow-data.

name: Outline to territory
purpose: Draw a country's outline then reveal its fill and name
looks_like: Navy screen: a country silhouette (the USA, filled blue with white edge) with big white condensed title 'COUNTRY NAME' above.
use_when: 'It started in the United States.' -> country
'Japan had never lost a war on its own soil, until 1945.' -> country
'The scandal swept across Brazil within a week.' -> country
avoid_when: No country in the sentence; a city or a region (use city-marker).
Several countries (use country-outlines or border-story); a beat under 3 s.

name: Time stamp
purpose: Establish a specific clock time over footage
looks_like: Landscape photo with a small yellow rounded badge at the top reading '07:11' and a black date strip 'JUNE 5, 1980' under it.
use_when: 'At 7:11 on the morning of June fifth, the first call came in.' -> date (+ time) + photo:1 (footage)
'The market opened at 9:30 and by 9:45 the stock was down twelve percent.' -> date/time + photo:1
'At 2:14 a.m. the lights in the studio went out.' -> date/time + photo:1
avoid_when: A date with no clock time in the sentence (use date-center or date-slide).
A photo where the top centre matters (the badge sits at the top, over the sky).

name: Date in space
purpose: Anchor footage to a large date and year
looks_like: Landscape photo with a centred white condensed day line '20TH OF JULY' and a smaller year '1980' below it.
use_when: 'On the 20th of July, 1980, the band played their last show together.' -> date + photo:1
'It was March fourth, 2021, when the first lawsuit landed.' -> date + photo:1
'On the 14th of April, 1912, the ship hit the iceberg.' -> date + photo:1
avoid_when: A year with no day and month (use year-slider); several dates in one sentence (use timeline_track).
date-slide does the same job with lighter, slower type; use date-center for the punchier condensed look.

name: Date arrival
purpose: Introduce an event with staged date typography
looks_like: Landscape photo with a big light sans date '02 July' and a bold condensed year '1975' under it, centred.
use_when: 'On the second of July, 1975, the studio finally signed him.' -> date + photo:1
'It was 9 November 1989 when the wall came down.' -> date + photo:1
'By 17 June 2015 the fund was already gone.' -> date + photo:1
avoid_when: A year only; several dates in one sentence (use timeline_track).
Versus date-center: slower, lighter, numeral-based (02 July); pick it for calmer documentary beats and chapter-like openings.

name: Case file board
purpose: Reveal a central subject surrounded by evidence and notes
looks_like: Cork-beige corkboard with a woman's portrait in the middle, red pins and red string to five surrounding photos (landscapes, an older portrait), white-bordered Polaroid look.
use_when: 'Detectives pinned the victim's face to the centre of the wall and strung every lead around her.' -> photos:6 (centre person first)
'At the centre of the scandal was one woman, surrounded by five people who all knew what she knew.' -> photos:6
'To investigators the suspect was the hub: his brother, his lawyer, his ex-wife, his business partner and the dealer.' -> photos:6
avoid_when: Sentence about a single person with no connected people or evidence; beats under 4 s.
When there is no central subject and the photos are just separate pieces of evidence use evidence-wall; case-board needs a main person to pin first.

name: Two perspectives
purpose: Compare two labelled images on equal terms
looks_like: Dark grid screen with two white-bordered images side by side, each with an orange label underneath ('LUNAR ECLIPSE', 'LUNAR PHASES').
use_when: 'The old stadium and the new one, same city, forty years apart.' -> photos:2 + list_items (two labels)
'The Instagram photo and the court exhibit do not match.' -> photos:2 + labels
'The original logo versus the redesign.' -> photos:2 + labels
avoid_when: Two people with names (use paired-profiles); no contrast in the sentence; beats under 3 s.
Pick this over diagonal-cards when the two things need a one-line name each.

name: People compared
purpose: Introduce two people with editable portraits and names
looks_like: Landscape photo background with two square portraits side by side, white capital names under each (SAMPLE PERSON A / B).
use_when: 'Taylor and Travis were seen together at the game.' -> photos:2 + two_names
'The two founders, Jobs and Wozniak, could not have been more different.' -> photos:2 + two_names
'Hamilton and Verstappen went into the last lap level on points.' -> photos:2 + two_names
avoid_when: More than two people; photos that are not portraits; a sentence naming only one person.
For black-and-white historical portraits use archive-profiles; for the same person then/now use age-comparison.

name: Archive portraits
purpose: Present historical identities with angled name strips
looks_like: Pale grey gradient with two square black-and-white portraits side by side, each with a black angled name strip in italic serif capitals underneath.
use_when: 'The two men who built the railroad, Collis Huntington and Leland Stanford, hated each other.' -> photos:2 + two_names
'Two detectives worked the case in 1974, Frank Hamer and Maney Gault.' -> photos:2 + two_names (old B&W photos)
'On one side, Churchill. On the other, Stalin.' -> photos:2 + two_names
avoid_when: Modern colour photos of living celebrities (use paired-profiles, same layout with a dark background).
Only one person named; sentence without two named people.

name: Trace a route
purpose: Explain movement between editable locations
looks_like: Dark map of North America with a red arc running from Los Angeles through a middle stop to New York, three dots.
use_when: 'He drove from Los Angeles to Las Vegas to New York, never staying more than a night.' -> place (2-4) + data
'The tour went from LA through Chicago to New York.' -> place + data
'The cargo travelled from Miami to Houston to Seattle.' -> place + data
avoid_when: Only one place; places not on one map; a sentence without a journey.
Needs route points; skipped without --allow-data. For a single flight use flight-route.

name: Archive film window
purpose: Place footage in a restrained archival frame
looks_like: Dark grid stage with one widescreen photo in a rounded window edged with small KODAK 400 film markings in the corners.
use_when: 'This is the last known photograph of the ship before it left port.' -> photo:1
'In the old family footage, you can see her laughing next to her father.' -> photo:1
'The only picture of the two of them together was taken in 1987.' -> photo:1
avoid_when: A modern phone photo or screenshot (the film frame reads as old stock); a graphic, chart or logo.
It is a frame, not a proof card: no text appears, so do not use it when a name or date must be read.

name: Vertical film reel
purpose: Sequence multiple moving image panels
looks_like: Dark screen with columns of rounded image panels (landscape photos and illustrations) sliding vertically like a film strip.
use_when: 'Her career in pictures: the sitcom, the first film, the Oscar, the divorce, the comeback and the book.' -> photos:6
'Over the years the city changed, and the postcards tell the story.' -> photos:6
'Scene after scene, the footage showed the same car.' -> photos:6
avoid_when: A sentence about one picture; beats under 4 s.
Pictures must work small (about a quarter of the frame each); if the pictures need to be read, use photo-collage or photo-stack. No text appears.

name: Travelling photo timeline
purpose: Move through successive illustrated milestones
looks_like: Dark screen with a row of four photos on a red progress line with white dots, a label under each ('FOURTH TEXT', 'FIFTH TEXT', 'NEXT'), the row sliding past.
use_when: 'In 2008 she got her break, in 2012 her first Emmy, in 2016 the marriage and in 2020 the split.' -> photos:6 + list_items (labels with years)
'Founded in a garage in 1976, listed in 1980, nearly bankrupt in 1997, back on top in 2001.' -> photos:6 + list_items
'The driver won his first race in 1998, his first title in 2001 and his tenth in 2010.' -> photos:6 + list_items
avoid_when: Fewer than three milestones; milestones with no photos (use timeline_track or milestone-path).
Prefer timeline_track when dates are the point; this one is better when the photos are the point.

name: Symbol lineup
purpose: Introduce several editable flags or logos in sequence
looks_like: Landscape photo background with a small condensed title at the top and four flags in a row (UK, France, Russia, Italy).
use_when: 'Four countries sent teams: Britain, France, Russia and Italy.' -> photos:4 (flags) + country + headline
'The deal needed signatures from Germany, Japan, Brazil and India.' -> photos:4 (flags) + country
'Sponsors from four nations backed the league.' -> photos:4 (logos or flags)
avoid_when: Fewer than three countries or brands; countries with no flag image available.
To compare logos on a plain background use brand-row; this one needs the photo behind it to look finished.

name: Featured image card
purpose: Lift a labelled image from its background
looks_like: Landscape photo blurred and washed out as a backdrop, with the sharp copy of the same photo lifted forward as a card in the centre and a white label strip under it ('Product Name').
use_when: 'The product at the centre of the lawsuit was a seventy-dollar blender.' -> headline + photo:1
'The painting, titled Salvator Mundi, sold for 450 million dollars.' -> headline + photo:1
'Meet the Model Y, the car that saved the company.' -> headline + photo:1
avoid_when: A person photo with a long caption; label text over about 25 characters.
For a person with a title use subject-headline or subject-pointer; feature-card suits an object, product or artwork.

name: Subject with headline
purpose: Put a foreground subject in front of a large editable title
looks_like: Landscape photo with a huge white condensed headline at the top ('FIRST FIRES') and a cut-out portrait standing in front of the lower half of the title.
use_when: 'Justin Baldoni: the director who sued everyone.' -> headline + photo:1 (cut-out person)
'Steve Jobs returns to Apple.' -> headline + photo:1
'The rookie who rewrote the record books.' -> headline + photo:1
avoid_when: A photo with a busy background (needs a clean cut-out); a long title; no person in the sentence.
Versus legacy-title (one word behind) and subject-pointer (label to the side): this is the magazine-cover look.

name: Question spotlight
purpose: Focus the viewer on a short question
looks_like: Landscape photo dimmed, with one short question ('What happened?') in a yellow highlight box in the middle.
use_when: 'So what really happened that night?' -> headline (short question) + photo:1
'Why did the board say nothing?' -> headline + photo:1
'Who was the mystery buyer?' -> headline + photo:1
avoid_when: Statements; questions longer than about 8 words; any sentence with figures.
Hold it for the question beat only, not the answer; works best at 3 to 5 s.

name: Year slider
purpose: Move along a time axis and resolve to a year
looks_like: Landscape photo darkened with a thin horizontal timeline and a white dot sliding to a bold year ('2025').
use_when: 'By 2025, nothing was left of the company.' -> year + photo:1
'It was 1998 when the first trailer dropped.' -> year + photo:1
'Then came 2016.' -> year + photo:1
avoid_when: A full date (use date-center or date-slide); several years in a sentence (use timeline_track); a year that is just a number in the sentence (a count, a price).
The slide takes about 2 s: put it at the start of the sentence.

name: World alert
purpose: Show a spreading issue across locations
looks_like: Dark screen with a white world map, four red pulsing dots (US, Europe, Asia, Australia) and a red banner 'GLOBAL SPREAD'.
use_when: 'The virus was in forty countries within a month.' -> place (several) + data (points)
'The outbreak spread from Wuhan to Italy to New York.' -> place + data
'Hackers hit banks on four continents in one night.' -> place + data
avoid_when: A story set in one place; any sentence without a spread or a count of places.
Needs data (points); skipped without --allow-data. The red banner suits alarms and outbreaks; not for celebrity news.

name: Drawn emphasis
purpose: Animate a hand-drawn loop around a key phrase
looks_like: Grey vignette screen with a yellow 'HELLO' label and small caption under it, a dark hand-drawn loop being scribbled around it.
use_when: 'And then the word everybody was waiting for: sorry.' -> text (one key word or short phrase)
'The one thing she never said was no.' -> text
'Nobody could explain why the deal was so cheap.' -> text (the key phrase)
avoid_when: Anything with a figure, name or list; text over about 4 words; serious sentences about victims.
Playful look: fits entertainment and sports commentary better than somber true crime.

name: Money and meaning
purpose: Count to an amount then explain its significance
looks_like: Landscape photo darkened, with a huge white condensed '$5.50' that counts up, and a condensed caption 'PER DAY ON AVERAGE' under it.
use_when: 'Judge Liman handed her four hundred and seven thousand dollars.' -> money + photo:1
'The company was fined 400 million dollars.' -> money + photo:1
'Fans spend five dollars fifty a day at the track on average.' -> money + photo:1
avoid_when: Anything that is not money (use number_glow for plain numbers, percentage-ring for percents); two figures in one sentence (use two-bars or value-table).
In the Windows test it printed '$400.0M' for 400 million; pass a number that displays cleanly. number_glow lands full-frame on the exact word; money-counter keeps the photo behind and counts.

name: Headline build
purpose: Reveal a compact multiline statement
looks_like: Landscape photo with a white sans headline built line by line, left of centre ('Sample Co. Reports $2.5 Million In New Sales').
use_when: 'Sample Co. reports 2.5 million dollars in new sales, and every analyst was wrong.' -> headline (3 short lines) + photo:1
'The studio pulls the film from theatres after one weekend.' -> headline + photo:1
'Judge rejects the offer.' -> headline + photo:1
avoid_when: A headline over about 12 words; a sentence with nothing to state as a claim.
Versus title-push (bigger, one phrase) and stacked-highlight (marker on key lines): headline-build is the plain statement of a fact.

name: Moving text marker
purpose: Highlight an editable phrase inside explanatory prose
looks_like: Landscape photo darkened, with a block of white sans text and yellow highlighter marker over the first phrase ('A spokesperson says').
use_when: 'A spokesperson says the team has found and logged a collection of fourteen thousand items.' -> text (sentence) + photo:1
'The contract states that she must not discuss the film.' -> text + photo:1
'The email read: we need to move the date.' -> text + photo:1
avoid_when: A sentence that is not a document claim; text over about 25 words.
Versus article-highlights (several highlights, paper look) and article-zoom (picture on top): this is the light overlay over footage.

name: Stacked highlight title
purpose: Build a phrase in separately highlighted lines
looks_like: Landscape photo with a two-line condensed black text on yellow highlight blocks stacked in the middle ('THE TRAGEDY / OF THE COMMONS').
use_when: 'This is what economists call the tragedy of the commons.' -> text (2 lines)
'It was, in the judge's words, a blunderbuss approach.' -> text
'The press called it the trial of the century.' -> text
avoid_when: Sentences with figures or names to show; text over about 6 words.
Loud look; versus headline-build (plain statement) and title-hierarchy (small setup + big last word).

name: Ranked bars
purpose: Compare ordered values with labelled bars
looks_like: Light grey screen with a title ('Top Countries by Sample Score') and five horizontal bars in different colours ranked from longest to shortest, country names on the left, a percent axis below.
use_when: 'The United States led with 90, then Britain, Germany, France and Japan.' -> list_items (3-6 labels) + number + data
'Of the five biggest studios, Disney made far more than anyone else.' -> list_items + number + data
'Top scorers this season: Haaland, Kane, Salah, Mbappe and Lewandowski.' -> list_items + number + data
avoid_when: Only two values (use two-bars); items with no measurable value; a sentence with nothing ranked.
Needs data; skipped without --allow-data. For people with photos use portrait-bars.

name: Before and after wipe
purpose: Reveal incoming media across outgoing media with labels
looks_like: Landscape photo on the top half with a yellow 'BEFORE' tag, a second illustration sliding up over the lower half with 'AFTER', separated by a thin yellow line.
use_when: 'Before the scandal she was America's sweetheart. After it, nobody would hire her.' -> photos:2 + two_names (labels)
'The stadium in 1990 and the stadium today.' -> photos:2 + labels
'Then, a sleepy village. Now, a city of two million.' -> photos:2 + labels
avoid_when: Two people to introduce (use paired-profiles); no change over time; always 2 to 4 s, rare, once or twice per video.
Do not use as a chapter break: the labels will show.

name: Icon and three points
purpose: Explain a topic through an icon and sequential points
looks_like: Dark screen with a big yellow rocket icon in a ring on the left and three yellow bulleted lines in condensed type on the right.
use_when: 'The startup grew three ways: faster shipping, lower prices and a loyalty app.' -> list_items (3)
'There were three reasons the show was cancelled: ratings, cost and a lawsuit.' -> list_items
'The plan was simple: buy the land, change the zoning, sell to the developer.' -> list_items
avoid_when: Lists of one or two items; items that are whole sentences.
With a photo behind it use checklist-panel; with numbered stages use process-steps; this one is best for upbeat business or tech lists.

name: Process steps
purpose: Show a sequence of stages with editable icons and labels
looks_like: Dark teal screen with three white icons in thin circles (fuel pump, truck, rocket) in a row, each with a green label tag under it (FUEL, TRANSPORT, LAUNCH).
use_when: 'The scheme worked in three stages: buy cheap fuel, move it by truck, sell it at launch prices.' -> list_items (3 stages)
'Step one is the audition, step two the screen test, step three the contract.' -> list_items
'The money went from the donors to the shell company to the offshore account.' -> list_items
avoid_when: A list of unrelated facts (use icon-bullets); fewer than 2 or more than 5 stages.
Pick this over milestone-path when each stage has a clear object or icon.

name: Population counter
purpose: Build a crowd of symbols while counting to an amount
looks_like: Landscape photo with a dense field of about 350 small teal person icons over it and a yellow box in the centre counting up '350'.
use_when: 'Three hundred and fifty people were in the room when the verdict came in.' -> number + photo:1
'The town had a population of only 350.' -> number + photo:1
'More than 350 employees lost their jobs that day.' -> number + photo:1
avoid_when: Money or percent (the catalog forbids them); numbers over about 1,000 or under 20.
A figure that is not people. image-to-crowd is the same idea with a photo beside the crowd.

name: Article focus
purpose: Push into a source-style image and highlighted paragraph
looks_like: Grey background: large source photo on top with tiny 'EDITABLE SOURCE IMAGE' caption, below it an all-caps black headline with the first words highlighted yellow; the camera pushes into it.
use_when: 'A spokesperson says the team has found and logged a collection of 14,000 sample items worth close to 2.5 million dollars.' -> photo:1 + text (the sentence as headline)
'Court filings show the company shipped the faulty part to eleven thousand customers.' -> photo:1 (document or product) + text
'The magazine's cover story read: The Fall of the House of Windsor.' -> photo:1 + text (quote or headline)
avoid_when: A headline with no picture to show above it; very short phrases (it is a sentence-length card).
news-image gives the same proof with a source label and is the first choice when a source name is spoken; pick article-zoom when the sentence is long and the picture is the evidence.

name: Portrait value bars
purpose: Compare values associated with people or brands
looks_like: Dark grid screen with three vertical bars (small, red, tall purple) each standing on a square portrait and topped with a dollar figure.
use_when: 'The top earners were three actors: one made 974 thousand, one 64 million and one 156 million.' -> photos:3 + list_items + number + data
'Of the three drivers, Hamilton earned the most by far.' -> photos:3 + list_items + number + data
'The three CEOs took home very different pay packages.' -> photos:3 + list_items + number + data
avoid_when: Fewer than three people; values with no data; things that are not people or brands (use ranked-bars).
Needs data. The sample's first label is hidden behind the portrait because the bar is too short, so pick it when the values are reasonably different.

name: Image annotations
purpose: Connect an editable image to explanatory labels
looks_like: Dark screen with one photo in the centre and three thin yellow leader lines to short labels ('Key Evidence', 'Timeline Details', 'The Truth').
use_when: 'In this one photo you can spot three clues: the watch, the shadow and the open door.' -> photo:1 + list_items (3 labels)
'The blueprint shows the vault, the vent and the guard room.' -> photo:1 + list_items
'Here is what to notice in the contract: the date, the signature and the clause.' -> photo:1 + list_items
avoid_when: No single photo with parts worth labelling; labels longer than about 3 words.
Beat under 5 s (the lines draw in).

name: Photo collage arrival
purpose: Assemble several overlapping photographs
looks_like: Full-frame stack of four white-bordered tilted photos overlapping, some cut off at the edges.
use_when: 'Fans left flowers, candles and photographs outside the gates for days.' -> photos:4
'Her Instagram that summer was a blur of yachts, beaches, dinners and red carpets.' -> photos:4
'Soldiers sent home letters, snapshots and drawings from the front.' -> photos:4
avoid_when: A sentence about one photo or one fact; beats under 3 s.
No text appears: use annotated-collage if labels are needed, photo-stack when pictures arrive one by one.

name: Photo stack sequence
purpose: Reveal successive pictures as a growing stack
looks_like: Dark screen with white-bordered photos dropping one by one onto a tilted stack in the centre.
use_when: 'Photo after photo surfaced: the beach, the yacht, the dinner, the hotel lobby, the car.' -> photos:5
'The police pulled five pictures out of the camera roll.' -> photos:5
'Fans kept sending in their photos of that night.' -> photos:5
avoid_when: A sentence about one picture; no text can be shown.
Min 5 s: pictures arrive one at a time. For overlapping spread-out photos use photo-collage.

name: Focus window
purpose: Keep a chosen subject sharp while de-emphasizing its surroundings
looks_like: Landscape photo heavily blurred except a sharp circular window in the centre, with a white label 'FOCUS' at the bottom.
use_when: 'Look closely at the man standing behind the driver.' -> photo:1 + title word
'This is the exact spot where the money changed hands.' -> photo:1
'Zoom in on the logo on the jacket and you can see the problem.' -> photo:1
avoid_when: A photo with no one detail to look at; when a lens must enlarge the pixels use image-magnifier.
It sets the focus point with focusX/focusY: only use when you know where in the picture the subject is.

name: Moving image loupe
purpose: Enlarge the actual pixels underneath a travelling lens
looks_like: Dark screen with one photo in a white frame and a magnifying glass sweeping over it, showing the area under the lens enlarged.
use_when: 'Zoom in on the corner of the receipt and you can read the date.' -> photo:1
'Blow the photo up and you can make out the number plate.' -> photo:1
'Under a magnifying glass, the signature did not match.' -> photo:1
avoid_when: A sentence with no detail to find in the picture; photos with too little resolution.
Picks proof over decoration; text-only 'magnifier' use is text-magnifier.

name: Diagonal image entrance
purpose: Bring two image cards into a diagonal comparison
looks_like: Light grid background with two rounded image cards on a diagonal, a wide landscape photo lower left and a flat mountain illustration upper right.
use_when: 'On one side, the old studio system. On the other, the streaming giants.' -> photos:2
'The home kit and the away kit, side by side, could not look more different.' -> photos:2
'The pitch deck looked nothing like the product that shipped.' -> photos:2
avoid_when: No contrast in the sentence; more than two things.
Pick paired-images for labelled equal images; diagonal-cards has no labels and is quieter. Beat under 3 s looks rushed.

name: Photo flip transition
purpose: Turn from outgoing image to incoming image
looks_like: Dark screen: a white-bordered tilted photo turns over with a see-through card sweep to reveal a second picture (a mountain illustration) in the sample.
use_when: 'That was the old house. This is what stands there today.' -> photos:2
'Then the picture changed.' -> photos:2
'She looked like this in 1999, and like this last year.' -> photos:2
avoid_when: Any beat that needs a caption or label (none appears); more than two pictures; always 4 s long, so do not squeeze it into a shorter beat.
One or two per video; for a plain scene change use clean-dissolve.

name: Expanding portrait panels
purpose: Grow a portrait card into a row of editable panels
looks_like: Dark screen with three tall photo panels side by side with thin gaps, growing out from one portrait.
use_when: 'Three women told the same story: Maria, Jane and Kate.' -> photos:3 (portraits)
'The family had three sons, and all three ended up in prison.' -> photos:3
'Three witnesses saw the car that night.' -> photos:3
avoid_when: Fewer than three photos; more than three; no names appear on screen, so do not use when the names must be read (use org-chart).
Min 2 s; best at 3 to 6 s with three portraits.

name: Moving route marker
purpose: Animate an editable vehicle or subject along a path
looks_like: Dark map (Middle East in the sample) with a red curved line drawn from a pin labelled 'City A' to an arrowhead at the destination.
use_when: 'He boarded a flight in Tehran and landed in Dubai six hours later.' -> place (2) + data (route points)
'The jet flew from Miami to Havana without ever filing a flight plan.' -> place (2) + data
'The shipment went from Shenzhen to Rotterdam.' -> place (2) + data
avoid_when: Only one place; the journey is not the point.
Needs route points (data); skipped without --allow-data. For several stops use route-line.

name: Milestone journey
purpose: Travel along a curved path of labelled milestones
looks_like: Dark screen with a curved yellow-to-grey line wave carrying numbered dots (04, 05, 06) each with a white label (Success, Next Stage, Complete).
use_when: 'First the pilot, then the funding round, then the launch, then the first million users.' -> list_items (3-5 stages)
'Her path: the audition, the breakout role, the Oscar nomination, the fall.' -> list_items
'The case moved from arrest to indictment to trial to a surprise plea.' -> list_items
avoid_when: Stages with dates (use timeline_track or photo-timeline); fewer than three steps.
No pictures here: use process-steps when icons help, milestone-path when the sentence is about a journey.

name: Connected before and after
purpose: Relate two stages with a connector and editable media
looks_like: Landscape photo with two dark framed boxes labelled 'BEFORE' and 'AFTER' linked by a dashed line.
use_when: 'Before the fame she lived with her mum. After the movie she owned three houses.' -> two_names (before/after labels) + photo:1
'Before the merger the firm had 4,000 staff; after it, just 900.' -> two_names + photo:1
'Before the crash, the car was a showpiece. After, it was scrap.' -> two_names + photo:1
avoid_when: Two people to compare (use paired-profiles); sentences with no clear first-then-second contrast.
The boxes are label slots over one photo; with two photos use paired-images or split-reveal.

name: Clean subject change
purpose: Replace a scene smoothly with a second scene
looks_like: Two-image transition: a flat illustrated mountain-and-sun scene fills the frame (this is the incoming scene).
use_when: Between two chapters of a documentary: 'And that was only the beginning.' -> photos:2
Hand-off from the setup to the story: 'But to understand why, you have to go back to 1998.' -> photos:2
Move from the courtroom to the aftermath: 'Six months later, nothing had changed.' -> photos:2
avoid_when: Any sentence that carries content; it shows nothing but the two pictures. Max one or two per video.
Not on a beat under 2 s; prefer split-reveal when there are labels and a harder cut.

name: Narration-paced caption
purpose: Reveal words in sequence over footage
looks_like: Landscape photo with one line of all-caps condensed white captions at the lower third, revealed word by word.
use_when: 'You have to understand what they were up against.' -> text + photo:1 (footage or photo behind)
'The tape runs for forty seconds, and nobody speaks.' -> text + photo:1
'He never saw it coming.' -> text + photo:1
avoid_when: Any sentence with a figure, name, place or list in it: use the piece for that. Caption on every beat reads as filler.
When the sentence is a verbatim quote use quote_card; it adds no information beyond the spoken words.

name: Editorial headline and column
purpose: Build a source-like headline and paragraph layout
looks_like: Light grey screen with a black rule on top, a headline in white serif caps on black bars, and a serif newspaper paragraph underneath.
use_when: 'The Times wrote that residents were angry at the plan but forgiving of the mayor.' -> headline + text (the paragraph)
'The Wall Street Journal reported the board knew about the losses in March.' -> headline + text
'In its report the Guardian said the club had paid the agent twelve million pounds.' -> headline + text
avoid_when: No outlet or report is cited and there is no wording to show; a photo is the proof (use news-image).
Beat under 3 s; no picture appears here, so use news-image or press-stack if the sentence names a source and has a photo.

name: Caption on grid
purpose: Present timed words on a clean graphic stage
notes: A dark grid whose words build over the piece: keep it to about 6 s and never on a beat longer than 9 s (the stage sits mostly empty).
looks_like: Dark grid stage with a single line of all-caps condensed white narration text built word by word in the middle.
use_when: 'And that is where the number appeared.' -> text (the spoken words)
'Nobody saw it coming, not the fans, not the owners, not even the driver.' -> text
'Then the phone rang.' -> text
avoid_when: Any beat over 9 s: the stage sits mostly empty; do not use as default filler, it carries no information beyond the words.
A sentence that has a person, place, number or list in it; use that piece instead.

name: News image bulletin
purpose: Pair an editable source label and headline with an image
looks_like: Dark grid screen with a red 'NEWS' tag, a yellow condensed headline 'LOCAL BAKERY OPENS THIRD SHOP AS LINES GROW', a date line and one photo underneath.
use_when: 'According to Variety, Lively received nothing for her claims.' -> photo:1 + headline (source label)
'TMZ published the video on Monday morning.' -> photo:1 + headline
'The Associated Press reported that the driver had been drinking.' -> photo:1 + headline
avoid_when: A claim with no outlet cited and no picture to show; a headline over about 10 words.
Use press-stack when several outlets are named; article-zoom when the sentence itself is the headline. This is the default for 'X reported that...' sentences.

name: People hierarchy
purpose: Reveal a leader and connected team members
looks_like: Dark grid screen with a title and subtitle at the top, a round portrait of a leader in the middle and four round portraits below connected by lines, each with a name.
use_when: 'Under the CEO sat four executives: the CFO, the head of sales, the general counsel and the product chief.' -> photos:5 + one_name + list_items (4 names)
'The family ran the whole operation, with four sons each in charge of a territory.' -> photos:5 + one_name + list_items
'The team around her was four people: her agent, publicist, lawyer and manager.' -> photos:5 + one_name + list_items
avoid_when: Fewer than three people; a person with no connected group; photos missing for the team.
With a brand at the centre use brand-hub; with money attached use wealth-network.

name: Sequential article highlights
purpose: Guide attention through several editable highlighted phrases
looks_like: Cream paper sheet on grey gradient: small 'FEATURE' label, big serif headline, a paragraph with several phrases marked in yellow highlighter one after another.
use_when: 'The filing says the studio knowingly misrepresented the budget and concealed the overruns from investors.' -> headline + text (2-3 phrases to highlight)
'The report calls the policy reckless and without precedent in modern banking.' -> headline + text
'The statement admits the team failed to report the injury for three weeks.' -> headline + text
avoid_when: Sentence has no quotable wording from a document; a photo is the proof (use news-image or article-zoom).
Beat under 4 s (highlights are sequential); when only one phrase matters use paragraph-marker.

name: Numbered chapter
purpose: Introduce a section with a large outline numeral
looks_like: Dark screen with a huge faint outline numeral behind a bold white word 'Number', a thin underline and a one-line white subtitle.
use_when: 'Chapter 3. The Deal.' -> number + headline
'Part two: The Cover-Up.' -> number + headline
'Number five on our list: the fastest lap in history.' -> number + headline
avoid_when: The catalog marks it buildable:false (the builder has no text for its chapter key); the planner skips it. Use chapter-opening or chapter-type.
Not for a sentence that is not a section heading.

name: Place callout
purpose: Pin and label a specific position on a map or aerial image
looks_like: Full-frame aerial city map with a yellow ring pin on one spot and a big white condensed label 'RIVERSIDE DISTRICT' with an underline beside it.
use_when: 'The shooting took place in the Riverside District, a block from the courthouse.' -> place + photo:1 (aerial/map)
'The company's first factory was in the old port quarter of Genoa.' -> place + photo:1
'The stadium sits in the middle of Midtown.' -> place + photo:1
avoid_when: A sentence with no named place; a photo that is not a map or aerial.
Versus map-circle (rings an area, label bottom-left) and city-marker (title, darker): use map-callout for a single point, map-circle for a neighbourhood.

name: Then and now
purpose: Explain a change between two replaceable subjects
looks_like: Dark screen with two square portraits side by side (young woman left, older woman right) and a yellow arrow between them; names/labels go under the pictures.
use_when: 'Ten years ago she was an unknown waitress. Today she is the most photographed woman in Hollywood.' -> photos:2 + two_names (same person, then and now)
'In 1962 the young senator looked like a fresh start; by 1974 he looked like a man carrying a country.' -> photos:2 + two_names (labels with the years)
'Before the transformation she was 280 pounds. This is her now.' -> photos:2 + two_names (before / after labels)
avoid_when: Two different people who are not a before/after of one subject (use paired-profiles); a single photo.
A sentence with no change over time; when the contrast is two rivals, not two ages, use paired-profiles.

name: Aerial camera move
purpose: Move across a replaceable map or aerial background
looks_like: Full-frame top-down aerial map of a coastal city (rivers, bridges, harbour, rooftops) with a slow push/pan across it; title text can appear over it.
use_when: 'The raid happened in a quiet harbour district on the edge of the city.' -> photo:1 (aerial or map image) + place
'Rome in its prime sprawled across seven hills and both banks of the Tiber.' -> photo:1 (aerial/map image) + place
'The company built its first data centre on an empty industrial lot outside Dublin.' -> photo:1 (aerial image) + place
avoid_when: Any sentence with no place in it; the picture must be a real aerial or map image, a portrait or logo looks wrong.
Beat under 3 s (the push is slow); when you need a pin or a circle on one spot use city-marker, map-callout or map-circle instead.

name: News lower third
purpose: Reveal a topic banner at the bottom of footage
looks_like: Landscape photo with a white banner across the bottom holding a big black condensed headline ('MIND OVER MUSCLE') and a small red 'BREAKING NEWS' tag above it.
use_when: 'Breaking: the judge has ruled.' -> headline + photo:1 (footage)
'The studio calls it a misunderstanding.' -> headline (3-4 words) + photo:1
'Here is the topic: the Blunderbuss Approach.' -> headline + photo:1
avoid_when: A name tag for a person (use circled-caption or subject-pointer); headlines over about 6 words.
Keeps the footage fully visible, so it is the best choice over real footage when you only want a topic title.

name: Checklist panel
purpose: Bring a checklist into footage and tick items in sequence
looks_like: Landscape photo with a cream card on the right: green tag 'BULLET POINT OVERLAY' and three ticked items ('Key takeaway one/two/three').
use_when: 'Three things every investor should check: the cash flow, the debt and the founder's track record.' -> list_items (3) + photo:1
'Prosecutors said the plan had three steps: steal the code, sell it, vanish.' -> list_items + photo:1
'Here is what you need to do: sign up, upload your script and hit render.' -> list_items + photo:1
avoid_when: A list of one or two items; list items that are long sentences (labels must be short).
When the list should appear as numbered stages with icons use process-steps; icon-bullets is the full-frame version without a photo.

name: Name and life dates
purpose: Identify a subject with name and date range
looks_like: Landscape photo with a centred condensed name ('SAMPLE NAME') and a smaller dates line ('1900-1980') beneath it.
use_when: 'Elvis Presley, 1935 to 1977, never gave an interview about that night.' -> one_name + year + photo:1
'Dale Earnhardt, 1951 to 2001, drove the black number three.' -> one_name + year + photo:1
'Ted Bundy, born 1946, executed 1989.' -> one_name + year + photo:1
avoid_when: A living person with no end year; a person whose years are not spoken.
No birth/death or career range in the sentence; use circled-caption or ribbon-profile to name a person without dates.

name: Opening chapter
purpose: Introduce a chapter with layered title and subtitle
looks_like: Pale grey vignette screen with a large dark sans title ('The Beginning') and a smaller serif subtitle under it, no photo.
use_when: 'Chapter one: how a small-town waitress became a pop star.' -> headline (+ subtitle)
'Part three. The collapse.' -> headline
'Round two: the leaked emails.' -> headline
avoid_when: Mid-section sentences; it is a section opener only, and only when the script has a heading.
Light, calm look and min 5 s; for a dark video or a title with no subtitle use chapter-type.

name: Changing phrases
purpose: Swap short statements at controlled times
looks_like: Landscape photo with one short line of all-caps white condensed text ('I AM STILL LEARNING.') in the centre, swapping to the next phrase at timed moments.
use_when: 'No lawyers. No publicists. No script.' -> list_items (2-4 short phrases)
'He said three things in the interview: sorry, never again, and I'm still learning.' -> list_items
'Nothing in the contract. Nothing in the email. Nothing in the deal.' -> list_items
avoid_when: Sentences with only one phrase; phrases over about 6 words; lists that need icons.
Plain and low in energy; use it for short rhythmic phrases, not for facts. Used once in the Windows test for 'nothing' x3.

name: Radial tool network
purpose: Connect a central concept to surrounding editable icons
looks_like: Dark grid screen with a teal logo hub in the centre and seven teal icon nodes around it joined by yellow lines, each node named (Writing, Research, Images, Editing, Voice, Video, Design, Planning).
use_when: 'The platform does everything: writing, research, images, editing, voice and video.' -> photos:6 + one_name + list_items (6-8 labels)
'The cartel's reach went into transport, banking, retail, politics and the police.' -> photos:6 + one_name + list_items
'Her brand spans perfume, skincare, clothing, a restaurant and a podcast.' -> photos:6 + one_name + list_items
avoid_when: Fewer than four spokes; spokes that are people (use org-chart).
Icons are generic; when a leader and portraits matter use org-chart or wealth-network.

name: Typed chapter heading
purpose: Type a chapter title onto a graphic background
looks_like: Dark grid stage with one large white title ('Chapter Title') that types on, no other elements.
use_when: 'Chapter four: the verdict.' -> headline
'Section two, the money trail.' -> headline
'The aftermath.' -> headline (one to four words)
avoid_when: Mid-section sentences; titles longer than about five words.
Pick it over chapter-opening when the video's look is dark and the section has no subtitle.

name: Paper typewriter
purpose: Reveal editable type on a moving sheet of paper
looks_like: Cream paper filling the screen with a very large dark serif title typing out ('Book Histor...'), typewriter keys fanned along the bottom.
use_when: 'The note, typed on a single sheet, read: I did it.' -> text (the typed words)
'In his diary he wrote: Today I decided to leave.' -> text
'The headline of her first book was The Girl Who Waited.' -> text
avoid_when: Long text (it is a big title, keep to about six words); a modern tech or data sentence; sentences not about something written.
It is a title card with no photo: do not use for a figure or a person's name.

name: Falling subjects title
purpose: Move replaceable objects through depth behind a title
looks_like: Dark screen with a huge serif white title ('SUBJECTS') while small dark cut-out objects (bombs in the sample) tumble through depth behind it.
use_when: 'The bombs started falling on the night of the fourth.' -> headline + photos:3 (cut-out objects)
'Money rained down on the crowd: hundred dollar bills, gold chains, champagne.' -> headline + photos:3
'Everything went wrong at once: the cars, the crew, the weather.' -> headline + photos:3
avoid_when: Objects must be cut-out images with transparent background; ordinary photos look wrong.
Beats where the title is long (one to three words only); serious sentences about real victims.

name: Subject callout
purpose: Point from a label to a replaceable foreground subject
looks_like: Landscape photo background with a portrait on the left, a big white condensed line ('AN INNOCENT') on the right and a yellow curved pointer line from the person to a small job-title text.
use_when: 'This is the witness, a bookkeeper who saw everything.' -> one_name + photo:1 (cut-out person) + title words
'Meet the CFO, the man who signed off on the numbers.' -> one_name + photo:1
'The goalkeeper, the only man who could have stopped it.' -> one_name + photo:1
avoid_when: No portrait; two people in the sentence; long text.
Pick subject-pointer when you want a role under a name; ribbon-profile when you only have a name; circled-caption over a full-frame photo.

name: Portrait behind title
purpose: Reveal a portrait against oversized background typography
looks_like: Dark screen with a huge dark-green serif word ('LEGACY') behind and above a standing cut-out portrait that rises under it.
use_when: 'Her legacy is complicated.' -> one_name + photo:1 + headline word
'He called it his masterpiece. History called it a fraud.' -> one_name + photo:1
'The King of Pop, 15 years after his death.' -> one_name + photo:1
avoid_when: A group photo or a face photo that is not cut out (the portrait needs a clean subject); sentences that give no title word.
Title word is one short word; when the sentence has a full headline use subject-headline.

name: Ribbon profile
purpose: Introduce a person with a colored graphic ribbon and name
looks_like: Dark screen with a square portrait on the left, a small grey 'PROFILE' tag and a crimson ribbon on the right holding the name 'ALEX MORGAN' in big white caps.
use_when: 'Meet Justin Baldoni, the director at the centre of the case.' -> one_name + photo:1
'Her name was Jane Doe, and she was last seen leaving the club.' -> one_name + photo:1
'Next up on the grid: Max Verstappen.' -> one_name + photo:1
avoid_when: A second person in the sentence; no usable portrait; a long title or role (the ribbon holds two lines of name).
Similar to subject-pointer, torn-profile and circled-caption: ribbon-profile is the clean TV-style intro; use it the first time a main character appears.

name: Paper-cut profile
purpose: Reveal a subject with a torn-paper name treatment
looks_like: Dark screen with a portrait on the left and a cream torn-paper label on the right holding a small red role tag ('The Antagonist') and a serif name 'SAMPLE NAME'.
use_when: 'Enter the antagonist of the story, studio boss Jeffrey Katzenberg.' -> one_name + photo:1 + role tag
'The suspect, a quiet neighbour named Gary Ridgway.' -> one_name + photo:1
'Her rival for the title: Serena Williams.' -> one_name + photo:1
avoid_when: A positive or neutral profile of a living celebrity; a role that needs more than two lines.
Its torn-paper look suits villains, suspects and rivals; ribbon-profile suits neutral intros.

name: Portrait and territory
purpose: Associate a portrait and role with an emphasized territory
looks_like: Dark map with a country (the UK) filled red and a portrait at lower left with a small 'Name and role' tag.
use_when: 'Queen Victoria ruled Britain for sixty-three years.' -> one_name + country + photo:1
'President Lincoln led the Union through the Civil War.' -> one_name + country + photo:1
'Prime minister Churchill refused to surrender.' -> one_name + country + photo:1
avoid_when: Any person who does not lead a country; no country in the sentence.
Versus regional-profile (any person tied to a region): use this one for a head of state or ruler.

name: Portrait quotation
purpose: Attribute an editable quote to a visible subject
looks_like: Warm beige split screen: left side a large serif quotation with a yellow opening quote mark and a yellow attribution line, right side a portrait of the speaker.
use_when: 'In an interview he said, I never wanted to be famous, I wanted to be left alone.' -> quote + one_name + photo:1
'The CEO told investors, We will not raise prices this year.' -> quote + one_name + photo:1
'She wrote on Instagram: This is not the end.' -> quote + one_name + photo:1
avoid_when: Paraphrase, not a verbatim quote; no portrait of the speaker; a speaker who is a group.
Versus quote_card (the narrator reads a verbatim quote word by word, no portrait): use quote-profile when you have a clean portrait and a 2-3 line quote; it is a full-frame layout.

name: Points to trend
purpose: Build data points and a connecting trend
looks_like: Light grey screen titled 'Generated Chart' with a thin black line connecting six dots rising steadily across 2000-2025.
use_when: 'Every five years since 2000 the number has gone up, from 4 to 70.' -> list_items (years) + number + data
'Subscribers grew steadily, from the early days to the present.' -> list_items + number + data
'Rents rose in a straight line for twenty-five years.' -> list_items + number + data
avoid_when: A trend with a dip, spike or two series (use single-trend or two-trends); no values.
Needs data. Lower weight than single-trend, which has a more finished look.

name: Two animated trends
purpose: Compare two labelled lines over time
looks_like: Dark grid screen with two zig-zag rising lines (blue USA, pink China) over 2021-2025, series names under the axis.
use_when: 'Chinese spending rose, but American spending rose twice as fast between 2021 and 2025.' -> list_items (years + two names) + number + data
'Her views climbed while his flat-lined all year.' -> list_items + number + data
'Ticket sales and streaming numbers moved in opposite directions.' -> list_items + number + data
avoid_when: One series (use single-trend); three series (use three-trends); no values.
Needs data; skipped without --allow-data.

name: Percentage ring
purpose: Count a proportion with an animated circular arc
looks_like: Dark grid screen with a blue ring about 72% full, '72%' in condensed white in the middle and a white caption tag below ('OF SAMPLE ITEMS').
use_when: 'That is five cents on every dollar she asked for.' -> percent (5) + caption
'Seventy-two percent of voters said they were undecided.' -> percent + caption
'Nine out of ten startups fail.' -> percent (90) + caption
avoid_when: Anything that is not a proportion of a whole; two percentages (use paired-pies).
number_glow also works for percent: use ring when the share of 100 is the point.

name: Cycle of ideas
purpose: Reveal connected stages around a circular process
looks_like: Dark screen with a thin white circle carrying four white round icons (globe, people, rocket, heart) at the compass points.
use_when: 'Success feeds itself: more users bring more data, more data brings a better product, a better product brings more users.' -> photos:4 + list_items (4 stages)
'The scandal fed on itself: every article led to a new leak, and every leak to a new article.' -> photos:4 + list_items
'It was a cycle: hype, funding, hype, funding.' -> photos:4 + list_items
avoid_when: A one-way sequence (use process-steps); fewer than 3 or more than 5 steps.
Min 5 s. The icons carry no labels in the still: do not use when each stage must be read.

name: City locator
purpose: Reveal a place pin and location title
looks_like: Darkened aerial map of a coastal city with a white map-pin and a small place label next to it; a big title ('Sample coastal c...') sits at the bottom.
use_when: 'It happened in Dallas, Texas, on a Friday afternoon in November.' -> place + photo:1 (aerial/map image)
'The company moved its headquarters to Austin.' -> place + photo:1
'He was last seen in Phoenix.' -> place + photo:1
avoid_when: No place name in the sentence; a place that is a country (use country-trace) or a whole region; place names longer than about 20 characters (the sample title is cut off).
Pick this over map-callout/map-circle when the sentence names one city and wants a title; the others mark a spot or an area on the picture.

name: Brand value table
purpose: Build rows of editable icons and values
looks_like: Landscape photo with a thin-bordered translucent table of four rows, each with a teal logo and a price on the right ($108, $58, $8.58, $78).
use_when: 'A burger costs 8 dollars at one chain, 58 at another, and 108 in a stadium.' -> list_items (3-5 rows) + number + photo:1 + data
'The three streaming plans cost 8, 15 and 22 a month.' -> list_items + number + data
'Compare the contracts: 12 million, 30 million, 45 million.' -> list_items + number + data
avoid_when: Only one or two rows; no brand or icon per row; values with no data. Min 3 s.
Needs data; skipped without --allow-data. Use ranked-bars when the length of the bars is the point.

name: Specimen comparison
purpose: Compare two cutout subjects with shared explanatory text
looks_like: Pale grey screen with two cut-out pictures side by side (a green frog and a brown toad), a serif title ('Frogs') and a grey subtitle under them.
use_when: 'The Ford Mustang and the Chevy Camaro look alike but are built very differently.' -> two_names + photos:2 (cut-out objects)
'Bitcoin and gold: two stores of value that behave nothing alike.' -> two_names + photos:2
'Two breeds, one gene: the greyhound and the whippet.' -> two_names + photos:2
avoid_when: People (use paired-profiles); photos with busy backgrounds; no comparison in the sentence.
Fits all niches for objects, products, animals; the catalog's fits (history, lists, sports) is narrow.

name: Two-value comparison
purpose: Contrast two quantities clearly
looks_like: Light grey screen titled 'School funding comparison' with two bars (pink $117M, black $271M) labelled 2019 and 2024.
use_when: 'In 2019 the district spent 117 million dollars on schools; by 2024 it was 271 million.' -> two_names (labels) + number + data
'Her salary was 2 million in the first season and 20 million in the next.' -> two_names + number + data
'Women's team revenue was 5 percent of the men's.' -> two_names + number + data
avoid_when: More than two values (use ranked-bars); only one figure; two people with photos (use portrait-bars).
Needs data; skipped without --allow-data. Always check the labels are short (2019 / 2024).

name: Chart over footage
purpose: Place a two-series chart over an editable background
looks_like: Landscape photo background with a dark rounded chart panel: title 'Data Comparison Over Time', two lines (blue falling, red rising) crossing on a 2020-2026 axis.
use_when: 'Cable subscribers fell every year since 2020 while streaming climbed past them in 2023.' -> list_items (years) + number + data (two series) + photo:1
'Her follower count doubled while his halved over the same six years.' -> list_items + number + data + photo:1
'Sales of electric cars overtook petrol cars in Norway in 2023.' -> list_items + number + data + photo:1
avoid_when: Only one series (use single-trend) or only two numbers (use two-bars); the script gives no values for the series.
Needs data; skipped without --allow-data.

name: Territory and symbols
purpose: Show organizations or flags associated with a region
looks_like: Dark map with one region (Iran) filled red and three flags (UK, Russia, UK) laid on it in a row, 'Sample region, 1900' at the bottom.
use_when: 'In 1907, Britain and Russia carved up Persia between them.' -> country + photos:3 (flags) + text
'Three powers had claims on the island: France, Spain and England.' -> country + photos:3 (flags)
'Foreign companies from four countries owned the oil fields.' -> country + photos:3 (flags/logos)
avoid_when: No country; a story about one power; flags you cannot source.
A history/geopolitics piece; the catalog fits are right.

name: Connected brand hub
purpose: Connect a central brand to supporting images
looks_like: Dark grid background: a teal app logo in a circle at the centre joined by yellow lines to four small circular photos above, below, left and right, each captioned 'Connection'.
use_when: 'Disney at the centre of it all: Marvel, Pixar, Lucasfilm and ESPN.' -> logo + photos:5 + list_items
'Every deal ran through one company, and it touched four other firms.' -> logo + photos:4 + list_items
'Her brand sits at the middle of a web of partners: a perfume line, a clothing label, a streaming deal and a charity.' -> logo + photos:5 + list_items
avoid_when: Sentence names no central brand or the brand has no logo available.
Sentence with a list but no hub (use icon-bullets); person-centred webs are better as radial-network or wealth-network.

name: Single growth trend
purpose: Draw a time series progressively across axes
looks_like: Dark navy screen with a clean white line drawing left to right over axes 2000-2010, y axis 0-700, '$ Billions' label at the bottom.
use_when: 'The company's revenue went from 80 billion in 2000 to over 600 billion by 2010.' -> list_items (years) + number + data
'Her followers climbed steadily every single year.' -> list_items + number + data
'Home prices rose year after year until the crash.' -> list_items + number + data
avoid_when: A trend with two or three series (use two-trends or three-trends); no real values; one number only (use number_glow).
Needs data; skipped without --allow-data. The most finished one-line chart; prefer it over scatter-trend.

name: Logo follows a trend
purpose: Move a replaceable brand mark along a data line
looks_like: Dark screen with a green line chart over 2021-2026 and a small teal logo riding the end of the line.
use_when: 'Tesla stock climbed from 2021, dipped in 2023 and ended the period up 40 percent.' -> logo + list_items (years) + number + data
'Her streaming numbers rose every year since 2021 and the label cannot explain it.' -> logo + list_items + number + data
'Revenue for the app doubled between 2021 and 2026.' -> logo + list_items + number + data
avoid_when: A trend for a person (use single-trend); no logo; no values for the series (needs data).
Only for brands; skipped without --allow-data.

name: Logo token reveal
purpose: Reveal a replaceable mark with dimensional scaling
looks_like: Dark screen with a single teal app logo sitting in a dark round disc in the centre, scaling up; no text.
use_when: 'Then Apple walked in.' -> logo
'The league's new sponsor is Emirates.' -> logo
'The company everyone was talking about was Theranos.' -> logo
avoid_when: No logo image; a beat that needs any words read; beats under 3 s.
logo-echo is the moodier version with a blurred copy behind; logo-token is the clean punch for a name drop.

name: Logo echo
purpose: Place a sharp mark over a large soft moving echo
looks_like: Dark screen with a sharp teal app logo in the centre over a very large soft blurred copy of itself.
use_when: 'And then Tesla made its announcement.' -> logo
'Netflix had one job: not to lose the audience.' -> logo
'Her new label is called Rhode.' -> logo
avoid_when: No logo image; a beat where something must be read (it has no text); beats under 3 s.
Pick logo-token for a crisper punch; logo-echo is the moodier reveal.

name: Brand and statistic
purpose: Pair a brand image with a numeric headline
looks_like: Full-frame landscape photo with a square teal logo on an orange tile at the top and a big orange banner reading '$42 MILLION IN SALES' below.
use_when: 'Peloton did forty-two million dollars in sales in the first quarter alone.' -> logo + number (+ money) + photo:1 (background)
'Her beauty brand pulled in ten percent of the whole category in its first year.' -> logo + number (+ percent) + photo:1
'The team sold 18,000 jerseys in a single weekend.' -> logo + number + photo:1
avoid_when: No brand or logo available; a figure with no brand attached (use number_glow or money-counter).
It does not anchor on the spoken number (anchor is sentence), so it suits a sentence where the brand is the subject and the figure is the supporting fact.

name: Brand lineup
purpose: Introduce several editable logos on a common baseline
looks_like: Dark grid background with three teal square logos in a row on one baseline, nothing else.
use_when: 'Netflix, Amazon and Disney all passed on the script.' -> logo + photos:3
'Ford, GM and Chrysler each lost market share that year.' -> logo + photos:3
'Nike, Adidas and Puma all pulled their sponsorship in the same week.' -> logo + photos:3
avoid_when: Fewer than three brands, or no logos to show; the brand names are not the point of the sentence.
When one brand has a number attached use brand-stat; when brands are ranked by value use ranked-bars.

name: Text magnifier
purpose: Enlarge editable text only underneath a moving lens
looks_like: Grey screen with a huge black word 'WELCOME TO OUR STORY' only legible inside a moving magnifying glass that sweeps across it.
use_when: 'Read the fine print: the clause says, in writing, we are not responsible.' -> text (a phrase)
'Hidden in the lease was one line: no refunds.' -> text
'The key word in the memo was reckless.' -> text
avoid_when: Anything that needs an image; text over about 5 words; a sentence that is not about reading something closely.
A reveal piece with no photo; use sparingly (weight 2). For text with a source page use article-highlights.

name: Place and image split
purpose: Connect geography to a picture of an event or object
looks_like: Dark map with one country region filled red on the left and a photo of an event or object sliding in on the right with a thin red edge.
use_when: 'In Oman, a single photograph changed everything.' -> country + photo:1
'The painting hung in a museum in Vienna.' -> country + photo:1
'This is the aftermath of the blast in Lebanon.' -> country + photo:1
avoid_when: A sentence with no country; a photo unrelated to the place.
For a country alone use country-trace; for a city on an aerial image use city-marker.

name: Image to population
purpose: Explain an image through a connected crowd of symbols
looks_like: Dark screen: an aerial photo on the left, an arrow to a grid of 39 grey person icons on the right with a counter below, one icon dimmed.
use_when: 'In that one building worked 39 people, and every one of them lost their job.' -> photo:1 + number
'This single village is home to 4,000 people.' -> photo:1 + number
'The raid on that house arrested 39.' -> photo:1 + number
avoid_when: Money or percent figures; a number over a few thousand reads poorly as icons.
A figure that is not about people; one photo is required.

name: Picture-filled area chart
purpose: Reveal a data area filled with an editable relevant image
looks_like: Light grey screen with a title ('Big increase in sample prices') and a green area chart whose filled area shows a landscape photo, a rising line 2003-2026.
use_when: 'House prices in the city nearly tripled between 2003 and today.' -> list_items (years) + number + data + photo:1
'Ticket prices have climbed year after year since 2003.' -> list_items + number + data + photo:1
'The studio's box office rose steadily from 2003 and then spiked.' -> list_items + number + data + photo:1
avoid_when: A trend with no real values; a photo unrelated to the topic. Only one series.
Needs data; skipped without --allow-data. Min 5 s.

name: Title camera push
purpose: Grow a short statement with controlled camera-like motion
looks_like: Landscape photo dimmed with one large white sans title ('Type your title here') centred, pushing in slowly.
use_when: 'This is the story of a man who stole a billion dollars.' -> headline (one short phrase)
'The trial of the decade begins.' -> headline
'Six days that shook the league.' -> headline
avoid_when: Sentences with figures to land (use number_glow), people to introduce, or lists; titles over about 8 words.
Plainest of the title cards: only when nothing more specific fits. Keep out of the video's first 5 s if a hook piece fits.

name: Price and direction
purpose: Link a price, replaceable object and directional arrow
looks_like: Light grey screen: lime tag '$0.50' with 'PER KWH' under it at top left, a big black arrow pointing down-left, and a stack of banknotes on the right.
use_when: 'Electricity there costs fifty cents a kilowatt hour, and the arrow points the wrong way for everyone.' -> money + photo:1 (object)
'A single ticket to the game cost 400 dollars.' -> money + photo:1 (ticket image)
'The painting sold for 90 dollars and is now worth forty million.' -> money + photo:1
avoid_when: A figure that is not a price per something; a percent; huge totals like 400M (use money-counter or number_glow).
The arrow points down: a price falling or the cost being pinned on something; avoid for a rising price.

name: Regional comparison labels
purpose: Reveal several countries with independent editable value labels
looks_like: Dark Europe map with the UK, Germany and Portugal filled red/purple, each labelled with a country name and a value (1.3%, 0.6%, 2.9%).
use_when: 'Unemployment ran at 2.9 percent in Portugal, 1.3 in Britain and just 0.6 in Germany.' -> country + list_items + number + data
'Of the shipments, Germany took 40, France took 25 and Spain took 10.' -> country + list_items + number + data
'Fans from Brazil, Argentina and Mexico bought the most tickets.' -> country + list_items + number + data
avoid_when: Only one country, or countries without a value; needs data.
When values are the story and not the geography, use ranked-bars; for plain outlines without values use country-outlines.

name: Colored territory outlines
purpose: Trace selected territories in different colors
looks_like: Dark Europe map where only the UK (yellow), Germany (pink) and Portugal (blue) are traced as thin coloured outlines.
use_when: 'Three nations signed the treaty: Britain, Germany and Portugal.' -> country + data
'The cartel stretched over Colombia, Mexico and Spain.' -> country + data
'These are the three countries that refused to play.' -> country + data
avoid_when: A single country (use country-trace) or a sentence with values per country (country-labels).
Needs data; skipped without --allow-data.

name: Statement hierarchy
purpose: Build a small setup phrase and large concluding word
looks_like: Landscape photo with a small serif setup line ('The Beginning of') over a huge white condensed word ('EVERYTHING').
use_when: 'This was the beginning of the end.' -> headline (setup + one big word)
'It was the biggest fraud in American history, bar none.' -> headline
'Welcome to the world of Formula One.' -> headline
avoid_when: Statements with no punch word; text over about 6 words; sentences with figures.
Use it when the last word carries the sentence; use headline-build for plain statements.

name: Population and callouts
purpose: Build a group of people and connect explanatory totals
looks_like: Dark screen with a 10x5 grid of orange person icons and two thin circled callouts either side, '65,000' left and '140,000' right.
use_when: 'The stadium held 65,000 people, but 140,000 turned up outside.' -> number + list_items (two or more totals)
'Attendance was 65,000 on Friday and 140,000 by Sunday.' -> number + list_items
'Of the 50 staff, 20 were laid off the same morning.' -> number + list_items
avoid_when: Money or percentage figures (catalog forbids them): a crowd drawn for dollars is wrong.
Beat under 4 s; a single total with no comparison (use population-count).

name: Annotated gallery
purpose: Arrange four photos and circle selected editable labels
looks_like: Black background with four tilted overlapping photos fanned out; two thin white hand-drawn ellipses circle text labels on the lower photos.
use_when: 'Investigators pieced it together from four things: a receipt, a parking ticket, a text message and a photo.' -> photos:4 + list_items (two circled labels)
'The trail of evidence ran through his yacht, his office, his mansion and his private jet.' -> photos:4 + list_items
'Her whole look came together from four influences: Audrey Hepburn, Twiggy, Bardot and Kate Moss.' -> photos:4 + list_items
avoid_when: Only one or two items in the sentence; a sentence with nothing to circle or label.
Beat under 5 s; if the photos are the point and need no labels use photo-collage, if six use evidence-wall.

name: Three growth curves
purpose: Compare three editable data series
looks_like: Light grey screen titled 'CHART TITLE HERE' with three rising curves (red, orange, blue) 1990-2025 labelled FIRST, SECOND, THIRD.
use_when: 'Netflix, Disney and Amazon all grew from 1990 to today, but Netflix grew fastest.' -> list_items (years + three labels) + number + data
'Rents, wages and house prices all rose, but only one outran the others.' -> list_items + number + data
'The three drivers' points totals climbed in step for twenty years.' -> list_items + number + data
avoid_when: Fewer than three series (use two-trends); series with no values.
Needs data; skipped without --allow-data; the labels sit at the bottom and are small.

name: Country to city zoom
purpose: Move from broad geography into a specific map image and label
looks_like: Aerial city map with a yellow pin ring and a black label 'Harbor district' joined by a yellow leader line (the start of the shot is a wider country map the camera moves in from).
use_when: 'From Italy to Genoa to one dock in the harbour, that is where the shipment vanished.' -> country + place + photo:1 (map/aerial) + data
'Across America, then down to Detroit, then to one factory floor.' -> country + place + photo:1 + data
'The trail runs from Mexico to a single warehouse in El Paso.' -> country + place + photo:1 + data
avoid_when: A sentence that names only a city (use city-marker or map-callout); map data is required, so it is skipped without --allow-data.
Do not use as a quick pin: it is a zoom-in move, 3 s at minimum.

name: Two proportions
purpose: Compare two animated percentages
looks_like: Dark screen with two pie charts side by side (30% yellow and 43% red) and a big percentage with a small caption under each.
use_when: 'Thirty percent of jobs are automated, and forty-three percent of workers have already been replaced.' -> percent (2) + two_names (captions) + data
'Forty percent of fans were over fifty, but only twelve percent were under thirty.' -> percent (2) + two_names + data
'Sixty percent of the jury believed her, sixty percent of the public did not.' -> percent (2) + two_names + data
avoid_when: One percentage (use percentage-ring); percentages with no caption; non-percent values.
Needs data; skipped without --allow-data.

name: Stack of press clippings
purpose: Build a stack of editable source articles and highlight a headline
looks_like: Grey screen with a pile of cream newspaper sheets, the top one tilted, with 'NEWS WIRE' and a big serif headline plus a paragraph.
use_when: 'Newspapers from the Times to the Post all ran the same story on Monday.' -> headline + text + list_items (outlet names)
'Within a day it was in every paper: the headline read Why Fears of a Market Bubble Are Growing.' -> headline + text
'Reports piled up from the BBC, CNN and Reuters.' -> headline + text + list_items
avoid_when: No report or outlet is named; a photo is the proof (use news-image).
Min 5 s. Prefer it over news-column when more than one outlet or report is cited.

name: Circled identity label
purpose: Identify a visible subject with an animated circled name
looks_like: Full-frame B&W portrait of an older woman with a white name label at the bottom ringed by a lime-green hand-drawn ellipse.
use_when: 'The woman in the photo, Edith Whitfield, was the only person in the building that night.' -> one_name + photo:1
'That man, Frank Abagnale, would go on to be the most famous con artist in America.' -> one_name + photo:1
'This is Bryan Freedman, the lawyer who has been on the other side from the start.' -> one_name + photo:1
avoid_when: Photo of a different person than the name, or a group photo; in the Windows test it circled a sentence chunk instead of the name, so pass the name only.
A name already shown by a lower third; when you want a larger portrait treatment use subject-pointer or ribbon-profile.

name: Area of interest
purpose: Circle and label a chosen region on a replaceable map image
looks_like: Full-frame aerial city map with a big thin yellow circle drawn around one district and a white condensed label 'DOWNTOWN DISTRICT' bottom left.
use_when: 'Police sealed off the whole downtown district.' -> place + photo:1 (aerial/map)
'The fire spread across the entire old quarter of the city.' -> place + photo:1
'Investors bought up everything inside that circle of Brooklyn.' -> place + photo:1
avoid_when: A single address or building (use map-callout); no place named; photos that are not maps or aerials.
The circle is large: do not use for a point location.

name: Subject and brand orbit
purpose: Connect a portrait to brands and an editable total
looks_like: Pale green screen with a portrait in the middle, four circled brand logos around it joined by green lines (Brand A-D), a faint '$1,100,000,000,000' total in the corner.
use_when: 'Bezos owns the Post, Whole Foods, Zappos and Blue Origin, and that is worth over a hundred billion.' -> one_name + photos:5 + money + list_items
'Her empire has four arms, and together they are worth a billion dollars.' -> one_name + photos:5 + money
'Every one of those companies traced back to one man and one fortune of two billion.' -> one_name + photos:5 + money
avoid_when: No total money figure; a person with fewer than three assets.
With no money use org-chart (people) or radial-network (icons); min 5 s.

name: Number Glow
purpose: Land one big figure full frame on the spoken number
looks_like: One big figure fills the frame and counts up, landing on the exact spoken number word; optional caption, prefix and suffix.
use_when: 'Judge Liman handed her four hundred and seven thousand dollars.' -> number (407000, prefix $)
'The suspect had been driving for fifty-two hours.' -> number (52, caption hours)
'The fund lost ninety percent of its value overnight.' -> number (90, suffix %)
avoid_when: A sentence with several figures, or a figure that is just background; beats under 3 s or a number landing within 0.45 s of the beat start (the count needs a pre-roll; pass count_s).
Max two per video and never twice in a row. In the Windows test it showed $0 until 0.45 s before the word: pass count_s = anchor time minus beat start.

name: Number Roll
purpose: Roll a playful yellow pill of digits up to the spoken number
looks_like: A playful yellow pill of digits spins up to the spoken number; money uses prefix $ and suffix M/K/%.
use_when: 'The film opened to $52 million in its first weekend.' -> number (52, prefix $, suffix M)
'Mourners lined up for 12 miles.' -> number (12)
'Her follower count hit 40 million in a week.' -> number (40, suffix M)
avoid_when: Single-digit figures (use number_glow); serious, somber sentences; two figures in the beat.
Lighter and more playful than number_glow; pick it for entertainment and sports, not crime or tragedy.

name: Prompt Card
purpose: Read an instruction, rule or definition along with the narrator over blurred footage
looks_like: Reads an instruction, rule or definition with the narrator over blurred source footage; needs the member's own 16:9 member's own video.
use_when: 'The rule is simple: never reveal the answer before the second act.' -> text + source_video
'In the prompt, tell the model: write in the voice of a nineteenth-century detective.' -> text + source_video
'The definition of insider trading is trading on information the public does not have.' -> text + source_video
avoid_when: The flow has no own video (the planner skips it without --source-video); a sentence with no wording to show.
Tutorial / how-to look; not suitable for celebrity news or crime.

name: Quote Card
purpose: Write a verbatim quotation word by word with the speaker named underneath
looks_like: Writes a verbatim quotation word by word with the speaker named underneath; needs the narrator to actually read the quote and name who said it.
use_when: 'The joint statement said the concerns raised by Ms. Lively deserved to be heard.' -> quote + one_name (or a source such as 'Joint statement, both legal teams')
'Churchill told Parliament: we shall never surrender.' -> quote + one_name
'The coach said afterwards, quote, we played like children.' -> quote + one_name
avoid_when: Paraphrase, not the exact spoken words; a quote with no named speaker or source; a quote under 5 s.
Versus quote-profile (portrait, full frame): quote_card goes over the cut and needs no portrait.

name: Key Flash
